info.title: Limitguard.ai
info.description: Lead validation API: the company behind each lead checked against the NL and BE business registers, EU VAT and sanctions lists, plus company, KYB and agent wallet checks for developers and AI agents

post.description:
Full entity trust check.

Always runs country risk and sanctions; runs each other data source
whose identifier is provided (up to 8 total), computes a trust score,
assigns a cluster, and returns a recommendation.

`entity_name` and `country` are required; identifiers (kvk_number,
cbe_number, domain, iban, vat_number, wallet_address) are optional and
raise confidence. With none, only country risk and sanctions run (plus a
KVK name search for NL), at lower confidence.

404.description: Not cached (X-Response-Quality: cached); no data source was called

post.description:
Deep check: extended PEP/RCA exposure screening, the Dutch insolvency
register on every tier, adverse media on the extended tier, an
Italian credit report on the credit tier.

`pep_extended` is the source the base check does not return. /v1/entity/check
queries the same OpenSanctions collection but filters to sanctions/enforcement
datasets and reduces the answer to a boolean (app/services/sanctions.py); the
role.pep/role.rca detail is fetched and discarded. This endpoint keeps it.

`insolvency_records` is the Centraal Insolventieregister (NL only; for any other
country the field says `applicable: false`). It is queried by `kvk_number` when
the body carries one (exact), else by `entity_name` (trade-name search).

`credit_report` is an Openapi.com credit score, Italy only, available when
OPENAPI_CREDIT_API_KEY is configured -- see /health. For any other country, or
a supported one with no `credit_report_identifier` (VAT number, tax code or
company ID) in the body, the field says `applicable: false` rather than being
omitted or erroring, the same pattern `insolvency_records` uses for non-NL, and
the `credit` tier's premium is never billed for it (app/middleware/x402.py
probes the country before pricing the call).

Three tiers, resolved from X-Response-Quality by the x402 middleware: `fresh`
(default; the `deep` tier, $0.88) returns pep_extended and insolvency_records;
`enhanced` (the `extended` tier, $1.71) adds `adverse_media` from dilisense;
`credit` ($2.45, Italy only, available when enabled) adds `credit_report`
instead. There is no cache-only branch, so `cached` is quoted, charged and
served as `fresh`. If a source of the requested tier cannot be reached the
answer is a 503 (`pep_source_unavailable`, `insolvency_source_unavailable`,
`adverse_media_source_unavailable` or `credit_report_source_unavailable`),
never a fabricated clean screen, and the x402 gate settles only on a 2xx so the
call is not charged.

503.description: A source of the requested tier is unavailable; payment is not settled

get.description:
Check current API key usage, the tier's real rate limits and prepaid balance.

Send X-API-Key header to identify the key. Free endpoint (no x402 cost).
`balance_usd` is the prepaid balance each priced call is debited from.
`rate_limit_per_minute`/`rate_limit_per_day` are the caps that actually
throttle calls (app.middleware.rate_limit.TIER_RATE_LIMITS); monthly_* is
a separate, looser abuse ceiling kept for backward compatibility.
With TIER_SUBSCRIPTION_ENABLED, `tier_expires_at`/`tier_queue` are the
active Growth/Pro term and the terms queued behind it (null otherwise).
`watch_recheck_credits` is the scheduled re-checks the key's Growth/Pro
purchases bought and it has not spent yet.

post.description:
Revoke an API key permanently.

The key being revoked is identified by the X-API-Key header.
This action is irreversible: the key stops working immediately.
Any remaining prepaid balance of a key that holds its own is forfeited; a key
that belongs to a workspace draws from the workspace balance, which revoking
the key never touches.

get.description: Get revenue attributed to a specific downstream AI agent.

WaaS endpoint: get USDC balance for an ERC-8004 registered agent.

`agent_id` is either the agent's wallet address (EVM 0x..., Base mainnet)
or a numeric ERC-8004 agentId. A wallet must be registered in the
configured ERC-8004 Identity Registry (one balanceOf call); a numeric id
must have been minted (ownerOf does not revert). Either shape that is
well-formed but not found answers 404; a malformed value answers 422.

Fails closed rather than quoting a balance it could not read:
503 wallet_registry_unconfigured when no registry address is configured,
503 wallet_rpc_unavailable when the Base read fails or the breaker is
open past its 24h stale-cache ceiling.

get.description:
De-listed compliance report: answers 410 Gone, charges nothing.

This route used to sell a "full compliance assessment for an entity", but it
returned the same EU AI Act briefing for every entity_id. There is no
per-entity AI Act data to build a real one from, so it was withdrawn. For a
readiness score from inputs you supply, use
GET /v1/compliance/readiness/{entity_id}.

The route is kept as a tombstone rather than deleted so an agent that still
holds the old listing gets a clear, machine-readable answer instead of a
bare 404. It is absent from ENDPOINT_PRICING_PREFIXES, so the payment gate
never quotes a 402 for it, and it takes no API key because the response
reveals nothing. Sandbox callers get the same 410: there is no mock either.

Once the per-entity report is live (enabled AND priced), the body also
points to POST /v1/reports/entity; while it is dark the body is unchanged.

CreditReportResult.title: CreditReportResult
CreditReportResult.description:
Result of the `credit_report` source, sold on the `credit` deep-check tier. `screened` is never False while `applicable` is True.

Mirrors InsolvencyRecordsResult, not AdverseMediaResult: coverage is a single
country (Italy), so "we do not cover this country" is a 200 with
`applicable: false` from app/services/credit_report.py, the same pattern the
insolvency register uses for non-NL -- never a raise, because that would be a
paid 503 for a caller who explicitly opted into this tier. A supported country
whose screen fails for any other reason (unset key, vendor outage, unparseable
verdict) still raises CreditReportUnavailable, and the router turns that into a
503 so the payment is never settled.

A green score is the provider's assessment of the company at query time, not a
guarantee of solvency and not a recommendation to extend credit. `risk_score` is
a normalised value from a closed set (green / yellow / red / unknown), not the raw
vendor string, and is None exactly when `applicable` is False; `risk_band_available`
is False when the provider declined to assess (its documented grey/ND answer, e.g.
a closed company), which is a different fact from a low-risk verdict.

CustomerUsageResponse.title: CustomerUsageResponse
CustomerUsageResponse.description: Complete usage response for customer dashboard (DYN-273).

kvk_number.title: Kvk Number
kvk_number.description: Dutch KVK number (8 digits); enables an exact insolvency-register lookup

credit_report_identifier.title: Credit Report Identifier
credit_report_identifier.description: VAT number, tax code or company ID for the `credit` tier's provider (Italy only today); without it the tier still runs but credit_report comes back applicable: false, same as an unsupported country

DeepCheckRequest.title: DeepCheckRequest
DeepCheckRequest.description:
Request for POST /v1/entity/deep-check.

Takes entity fields rather than an ``entity_id`` from a prior check: the audit
trail is keyed by sha256(entity_name) and is one-way, so an id could not be
resolved back to the name the screens have to query. ``kvk_number`` is optional
and only consulted by the insolvency source: the Centraal
Insolventieregister keys ``searchUndertaking`` on the KvK number, which is an
exact lookup where a trade-name search is a fuzzy one. ``credit_report_identifier``
is only consulted by the `credit` tier's source: Openapi.com's Italian
credit-score lookup keys on a VAT number, tax code or company ID rather than a
name, and reports back in `identifier_type` which one it matched.

quality.title: Quality
quality.description: deep (fresh), extended (enhanced) or credit; see DEEP_CHECK_TIER_NAMES. `credit` only resolves while OPENAPI_CREDIT_API_KEY is configured.

InsolvencyRecordsResult.title: InsolvencyRecordsResult
InsolvencyRecordsResult.description:
Result of the `insolvency_records` source.

Unlike PepScreenResult and AdverseMediaResult, `screened` CAN be False on a 200:
the register covers the Netherlands only, so for any other `country` the source
is not consulted and the row says so with `applicable: false`. That is a
different fact from a clean negative and must never be read as one. When
`applicable` is True, `screened` is always True: every other failure raises and
the router answers 503, so the caller is not charged.

A negative result (`found: false`) means the register listed no insolvency
proceeding for the KvK number or trade name at query time. Exception code 3
("too many results") is reported as `found: true, truncated: true,
match_count: null` with no records: matches exist but the register will not
list them until the query is narrowed (send `kvk_number`).

Register conditions: no replica is kept and a successful screen is cached for at
most 24 hours (app/config.py::cache_insolvency_ttl), inside the six-month
destruction rule the subscription imposes.

ValidationErrorResponse.title: ValidationErrorResponse
ValidationErrorResponse.description:
RFC 7807 body of a 422 request validation error.

The shape main.py's RequestValidationError handler sends, so a generated client
parses `detail` as the list it is, not as a string.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the VAT number was not checked or not valid. vies_unavailable: the EU VAT service did not answer, so it was not checked. invalid_format: the number is not in an EU VAT number format. non_eu_country: the number does not start with an EU country code.

pending_settlements.title: Pending Settlements
pending_settlements.description: Pending rows still inside the sweep's retry budget (in-flight). Rows the sweep cannot rebuild into a payment are charged the same budget, so they drain to exhausted_settlements rather than sitting here forever

exhausted_settlements.title: Exhausted Settlements
exhausted_settlements.description: Pending rows whose sweep_attempts reached MAX_RETRIES: credited, never settled, no longer retried. Not included in pending_settlements

failed_settlements.title: Failed Settlements
failed_settlements.description: Ledger rows the startup sweep resolved to FAILED. These are no longer counted by pending_settlements, so without this they would disappear from the health view entirely.

uncollected_usdc.title: Uncollected Usdc
uncollected_usdc.description: USDC credited to the ledger that will never settle: exhausted PENDING plus FAILED rows, excluding rows written off (, see written_off_usdc). Reconciliation work, expressed as money rather than as two row counts.

written_off_usdc.title: Written Off Usdc
written_off_usdc.description: USDC on ledger rows an operator wrote off as never settling: excluded from exhausted_settlements, failed_settlements and uncollected_usdc, summed here so the loss stays visible.

settlement_configured.title: Settlement Configured
settlement_configured.description: True when the EVM settler would run (SETTLEMENT_RPC_URL and SETTLEMENT_PRIVATE_KEY both set). EVM leg only; see solana_settlement_configured for the other leg. When False, EVM rows stay pending indefinitely

solana_settlement_configured.title: Solana Settlement Configured
solana_settlement_configured.description: True when the Solana settler would run (SOLANA_RPC_URL and SOLANA_FEE_PAYER_PRIVATE_KEY both set). All three settlement counters above are chain-mixed, so both flags must be read to know whether they are trustworthy. When False, Solana rows stay pending indefinitely

solana_fee_payer_balance_sol.title: Solana Fee Payer Balance Sol
solana_fee_payer_balance_sol.description: Fee payer's SOL balance, or null when solana_settlement_configured is false or the RPC read failed (not the same as a genuine zero).

solana_fee_payer_low_balance.title: Solana Fee Payer Low Balance
solana_fee_payer_low_balance.description: True when solana_fee_payer_balance_sol is below SOLANA_FEE_PAYER_LOW_BALANCE_SOL (default 0.05). Always false when the balance could not be read.

WalletRiskComponent.title: WalletRiskComponent
WalletRiskComponent.description: The wallet screen's own risk score and the named rules that fired.

rescore_interval.title: Rescore Interval
rescore_interval.description: Seconds between rescores. Applies only when change monitoring is switched on for this service; it is off by default. The service enforces a minimum interval (7 days by default).

country.title: Country
country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. With a country and at least one typed identifier, the entry is under change monitoring on plans that include it, when change monitoring is switched on for this service (then a weekly re-check, changes sent as identifier.change.new webhooks). It is off by default.

delivered_events.title: Delivered Events
delivered_events.description: Subset of `events` actually sent today; the rest are registrable but not yet emitted by anything

WebhookCreateResponse.title: WebhookCreateResponse
WebhookCreateResponse.description: Response for POST /v1/webhooks -- includes secret (one-time display).

source_label.title: Source Label
examples: on bol.com, company details page, next to its Chamber of Commerce number

register_number_on_page.title: Register Number On Page
register_number_on_page.description: The page also shows the company's own KVK/KBO or VAT number.

WebsitePhone.title: WebsitePhone
WebsitePhone.description: A phone number the company publishes on its website.
